passage:
Manoj sat on the balcony of the Andheri flat with his laptop, frowning at a bug that wouldn't go away. Siddharth came out with two mugs of tea and put one beside him. Manoj rubbed his eyes.

"Long day?" Siddharth asked. Manoj nodded.

"Can I?" Siddharth held his hand near Manoj's hair, not touching. "Only if you want it."

"Yes, please."

He ran his fingers lightly through Manoj's hair a few times. Manoj's shoulders dropped and he leaned in a little, eyes closing. After a minute Manoj said, "That's enough, thanks," and Siddharth stopped at once, squeezed his shoulder, and picked up the tea.

qa.q: What did Siddharth bring out to the balcony?
qa.a: Siddharth brought out two mugs of tea.

qa.q: What did Manoj's leaning in and dropped shoulders suggest?
qa.a: They suggested Manoj felt comforted and safe with the touch, after a long day. Manoj also said yes when asked, so the reading is backed by consent, not just by posture.

qa.q: What made this a caring way to offer a gentle touch?
qa.a: Siddharth asked first, kept the hand still until Manoj said yes, and stopped at once when Manoj said enough.

qa.q: What could Siddharth have done if Manoj had stiffened or said no?
qa.a: Siddharth could have pulled back, put the hand down and checked in gently about what Manoj needed instead.

grounding: A gentle stroke of hair conveys tenderness between partners, welcome because consent was asked and respected.

passage:
"Can I sit here?" Maria asked, dropping her bag on the sofa.
"Of course," said Simran. "Bad exam?"
"Awful. I froze on the last question." Maria's voice wobbled. "Is it okay if I put my head on your shoulder for a bit?"
"Sure. Come here."
Simran stroked Maria's hair a few times, slowly. Then Maria's shoulders tensed.
"Too much?" Simran asked, pulling her hand back at once.
"A little. Just sit with me instead."
"Okay. I'm right here."
They watched the rain run down the window for a while. Maria breathed out. "Thanks for checking. Sometimes I want closeness, sometimes I don't."
"I'll always ask," said Simran.

qa.q: What did Maria ask Simran before putting her head on the shoulder?
qa.a: Maria asked, 'Is it okay if I put my head on your shoulder for a bit?'

qa.q: Why did Maria's shoulders tense while her hair was being stroked?
qa.a: Maria felt it was a bit too much at that moment, and needed closeness without stroking. It shows a person can want comfort and still not want every kind of touch.

qa.q: What did Simran do that showed good care?
qa.a: Simran pulled the hand back at once and asked 'Too much?', then simply stayed beside Maria.

qa.q: How might Simran have felt when Maria said 'a little'?
qa.a: Simran may have felt a flicker of worry about having overstepped, but the quick adjustment and the promise to always ask suggest care rather than hurt.

grounding: A caress offers tenderness only with consent, and when a person stiffens, the other stops and checks in.

passage: Looking back at that week after Shalini's breakup, I think I learnt more about my little sister than in all our years sharing a room. The first night, I sat beside her on the bed and stroked her hair the way Amma used to when we were sick. She went stiff under my hand. Her shoulders rose. I pulled my hand back at once. "Too much?" I asked. She nodded without looking up. "Can you just sit?" So I sat, not touching, and she cried and talked. Two nights later she leaned her head on my shoulder herself, and after a while she said, "You can do the hair thing now." I did, slowly. She fell asleep like that. I, Keerthana, the big sister who fixes everything, had to learn that comfort sometimes means waiting.

qa.q: Whose way of stroking hair did Keerthana copy?
qa.a: The way Amma used to when they were sick.

qa.q: What was Shalini feeling when she went stiff under Keerthana's hand the first night?
qa.a: She seemed overwhelmed and not ready to be touched, though she still wanted company; two nights later she felt safe enough to ask for the hair stroking.

qa.q: How did Keerthana handle it when Shalini stiffened?
qa.a: She stopped at once, asked "Too much?" and stayed nearby without touching until Shalini invited it.

qa.q: What would change if Keerthana had kept stroking Shalini's hair that first night?
qa.a: Shalini might have felt crowded and less able to talk or cry, so the comfort would have felt like pressure.

grounding: Shows tender hair-stroking between sisters offered with attention to consent, stopping when the other person stiffens and resuming only when invited.

passage:
Ward nurse's note, women's surgical ward, night shift.
Bed 12, Zainab, 22, day one after her operation. Her husband, Yogesh, sat with her all evening. I noticed he kept stroking the back of her hand very lightly, and each time she settled and her breathing slowed. Around eleven her pain rose. When he reached for her hand, she pulled it away and turned her face. He froze, then took his hand back and asked quietly, "Do you want me to stop, or just be here?" She said, "Just be here." He sat back with his hands in his lap. I gave her the medicine the doctor had charted and checked her after half an hour. By midnight she held her hand out to him herself, and he took it. I reminded him visiting would end soon; he said goodnight softly. Will pass on at handover that the family is a good support.

qa.q: What was Yogesh doing that helped Zainab settle in the evening?
qa.a: He kept stroking the back of her hand very lightly.

qa.q: What was Yogesh feeling when Zainab pulled her hand away?
qa.a: He seemed startled and a little hurt, freezing for a moment, but his quiet question shows he cared more about what she needed than about being close.

qa.q: What does the nurse's note show about the right way to use gentle touch?
qa.a: It shows touch comforts only when welcome: Yogesh stopped at once when Zainab pulled away, asked, and waited until she offered her hand again.

qa.q: How did Zainab experience her husband's touch at different moments?
qa.a: In calmer moments the stroking soothed her, but when pain rose she needed space, and later she chose to reach out to him herself.

grounding: Shows gentle hand-stroking between partners as tenderness that depends on consent, with the partner stopping and checking in when she pulls away.

passage:
Thursday, late.
Manoj came over after the call from his dad. He sat on my sofa with his head in his hands and didn't say much. I sat next to him and, without thinking, started stroking his hair, the way he likes on lazy Sundays. He leaned into it for a minute. Then he went tense and moved his head away. I stopped straight away and asked, "Not now?" He said, "Sorry. I just feel like I'll fall apart if you're too soft right now." I told him nothing to be sorry for. I made tea instead and sat with my knee touching his, which he seemed fine with. Later, when he got up to leave, he hugged me for a long time, and said thanks for listening. I keep thinking: the same touch that helps on Sunday can be too much on a Thursday like this.
— Nazia

qa.q: What had happened before Manoj came over?
qa.a: The call from his dad.

qa.q: What was Nazia feeling when Manoj moved his head away?
qa.a: Nazia was probably a little startled, but mostly concerned for Manoj, which shows in stopping at once and gently asking "Not now?"

qa.q: What did Nazia do that respected Manoj's limits?
qa.a: Nazia stopped straight away, asked "Not now?", and switched to tea and a small knee touch Manoj seemed fine with.

qa.q: If you were Manoj, what would you want from a partner on a night like this?
qa.a: Someone who stays close but lets you set how much touch feels okay, as Nazia did, so you can hold yourself together.

grounding: Shows a gentle hair stroke between partners as tender affection that is stopped and checked when the other person tenses.
